text:
sam_support: Customer 8672 on EU SaaS plan reporting ~250-600ms extra latency and ~1% auth failures starting 08:10 UTC. They say traffic is landing in us-west instead of eu-west. Billing spike noted due to egress. Ticket CS-4128.
lee_sre: Can you paste the customer's DNS results and a curl with response headers? My hunch: resolver affinity / EDNS stripping causing wrong-pop selection.
nina_network: Also ask for traceroute from client to the resolved IP. ISP caches often keep stale mapping and can route to wrong POP for hours.
sam_support: Pasting what the customer sent:
```
# customer from Frankfurt
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai
34.120.10.5
$ curl -I https://api.redwood.ai -H 'Host: api.redwood.ai'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-pop: us-west-2
x-cache: MISS
x-request-id: abc-123
```
They also ran @8.8.8.8 -> same IP. They say it used to resolve to 34.247.200.12 (eu-west) until ~07:50 UTC.
lee_sre: Thanks. Two likely causes: 1) upstream resolver (ISP/EDNS) is returning an older cached A record pointing at a different anycast POP IP; 2) our GeoIP DB used for fallback routing was out of sync so fallback selected US. Can we confirm our geoip version on edge nodes and DNS TTLs?
nina_network: From checks here:
- edge-dns TTL: 60s for api.redwood.ai (we intended 60)
- GeoIP DB on edge-eu-1: version 2025.11 (we shipped 2026.02 last week to edge-us only due to a rollout flag)
- Some ISP resolvers in EU report broken EDNS client-subnet and sticky cache retention of 300s-3600s.
lee_sre: Ok that explains transient cross-region hops. Repro steps I want:
1) From a Frankfurt VM: dig @1.1.1.1 +trace api.redwood.ai
2) dig +nssearch api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8 @1.1.1.1
3) curl -v to resolved IP to capture x-pop, x-geo headers
4) traceroute to the IP
Please paste outputs.
sam_support: Customer provided traceroute snippet:
```
1  10.0.0.1
2  isp-gw.example 12 ms
3  198.51.100.45 28 ms
4  34.120.10.5 290 ms
```
So hops go to us-hosted IP.
lee_sre: Next actions:
- Roll GeoIP DB to edge-eu-1 now (rollback plan ready). Ill trigger update and monitor DNS answers.
- Add a temporary DNS answer override for customer IP block (very targeted) if they are enterprise and need immediate fix.
- Ask customer to flush their resolver cache or try a different resolver (Cloudflare/Google) as a short-term mitigation.
nina_network: I pushed geoip 2026.02 to edge-eu-1 (change id: roll/geoip/2026.02). Please verify with dig from their location.
sam_support: Ran dig after rollout (customer): now returns 34.247.200.12 and x-pop: eu-west-1 — latency back to expected ~40ms. Customer confirms auth failures stopped. :relieved:
lee_sre: Good. Root cause: partial geoip rollout + aggressive ISP resolver caching; combined with low TTL our intended rapid routing changes couldn't propagate to some resolvers. Mitigation items:
- QA: ensure geoip rollout completes to all edges before changing DNS-sensitive routing (assigned to nina_network)
- Policy: increase TTL to 300s temporarily for api records during geoip rollouts to reduce inconsistent answers (assigned to lee_sre)
- Support playbook: steps for customers to flush or test alternate resolvers and how to request targeted DNS override (assigned to sam_support)
sam_support: Noted. I'll update ticket CS-4128 and the customer. Close after 24h monitoring. :thumbsup:
devops-bot: deploy:roll/geoip/2026.02 completed on edge-eu-1 at 08:41 UTC
tim_customer_success: Thanks team — customer wants a post-mortem and cost rollback consideration for the egress spike. Can we estimate extra egress during 08:10-08:42?
lee_sre: I'll pull egress numbers and add to incident follow-up. Will also propose a short experiment: maintain a stable geoip version during traffic-sensitive windows.
